title: 21.6 A 2A Fully Analog Distribution LDO with Noise Immunity for an SoC
problem: Analog distribution LDOs (DISLDOs) for SoCs suffer from noise coupling on analog control signals between distributed power transistors, resulting in excessive output voltage ripple and preventing practical deployment in advanced SoCs.
motivation: As SoC complexity advances, thermal management requires current distribution across multiple spatially-separated power transistors, but analog DISLDO control signals are vulnerable to on-chip noise interference.
method: A fully analog DISLDO design incorporates noise-immune analog signal distribution and transmission techniques to maintain even current distribution across power transistors despite high on-chip noise, achieving 2A output current with stable regulation.
key_novelty: Noise-immune analog control signal distribution enabling practical analog DISLDOs in noisy SoC environments.
contributions: Noise-immune analog signal distribution for distributed LDO
2A fully analog DISLDO for SoC integration
Even current distribution across power transistors
Reduced static current vs digital DISLDOs
limitations: Abstract-only analysis; specific noise metrics, ripple measurements, and efficiency comparisons not provided.
primary_theme: Noise-immune analog distribution LDO for SoCs
